newsitem.title: USA: PointCast's Hassett says working with Tibco.
newsitem.headline: PointCast's Hassett says working with Tibco.

text.p: PointCast Chairman Chris Hassett said his company is working with Tibco Software Inc to incorporate real-time push capabilities into PointCast's Internet-based information services.

In early 1996 PointCast pioneered the concept of using so-called "push" technology as a means of delivering news, advertising and other information, personalized to individual's specific interests, over the World Wide Web.

Hassett told technology executives from financial services firms and other industries at Tibco's "Strategic Directions 97" that PointCast's original offerings were based on a "scheduled pull" method rather than push.
Engineers say this pull method increases traffic over networks as servers, which link together computer networks, must routinely contact central computers to retrieve updates.

"That's really not the ultimate and right way to do it. The right way to do it is really a truly real-time multicast scenario," Hassett said, adding PointCast spends roughly $250,000 a month on communications costs.

"Tibco as a company has really the best implementation that PointCast has found of the underlying capabilities of a true broadcast, a true multicast technology that's available on the Internet," he said.

Multicast capabilities enable an organization to send out messages to MANY people at once. Tibco says its technology enables data to be sent out in real time once, diminishing the load on computer networks, including the Internet.
Hassett said privately-held PointCast, which was founded in 1992 and has grown to employ roughly 250, from the outset viewed the Internet as a new medium, like radio or television.
"We're really not a technology company," Hassett said in a keynote address to the meeting. "We're really an information supplier. We're more of a service company."
PointCast ecently began a search for an executive to take over the chief executive post while Hassett remains chairman.

Earlier this month the company released an upgraded version of its product and Hassett said it is looking at providing both deeper content and information which is particularly relevant to the work profiles of its users.

PointCast, based in Santa Clara, Calif., has shifted more heavily to advertising as the basis of its business model and will give away its server software to companies willing to allow its advertising to be displayed.

The company plans to develop markets with vertically- oriented data for industries such as health care, real estate, petroleum, entertainment, insurance, banking, telecommunications and information technology, he said.
"Our goal going forward is to get more and more content that makes your employees smarter, makes your employees more productive," the executive said.

Hassett did not elaborate on details of the work between PointCast and Tibco. "I can't really commit to a time line," he said. "It's in active development.. I would expect that we can get this done very quickly."

Hassett said eventually he expects real-time push, through multicasting, will be as pervasive and simple to use as cable television or broadcast over the airwaves is currently, allowing people around the world to "tune in" regularly to talks from their executives, and other live information.
Tibco Software is a part of Tibco Inc., which was acquired by Reuters Holding Plc. in 1994. Cisco Systems Inc. announced last month it has made a minority investment in Tibco Software.
